name: 3D Surface
miniText: How can a moving point cloud suggest a smooth surface? NetLogo 3D Surface randomly samples horizontal coordinates and computes height from a time-dependent cosine expression. It displays the resulting three-dimensional points through an oblique two-dimensional projection and varies color with height. Computer graphics [1] grounds projection and visual depth cues; differential geometry [2] explains a surface defined as a height function; computational geometry [3] frames the difference between discrete samples and an underlying continuous object. Changing sample count or the height formula reveals how representation affects perceived continuity. The displayed wave is prescribed mathematically: no elastic forces or material equations generate it. Finite sampling and projection can hide structure or introduce apparent overlaps. The simulation illustrates coordinate mapping and animated parameterization, without validating membrane mechanics or a physical wave equation.
